title: Brute force attack on jsmith VPN account from malicious IP
summary: IP 185.220.101.47 performed 37 failed VPN login attempts for user jsmith within 10 minutes, then successfully authenticated at 02:18:24. The source IP is a known Tor exit node and credential-stuffing suspect with 412 reports. User jsmith is a Marketing Coordinator who does not normally work remotely, making the successful login anomalous.
evidence: 37 failed VPN login events from 185.220.101.47 for user jsmith between 02:14:00-02:18:16
Successful login at 02:18:24 from same IP, outcome: success
IP reputation: malicious, tags include tor-exit-node and credential-stuffing, 412 reports
User context: jsmith is Marketing Coordinator, works_remote: false, normal hosts WS-07/FS-01
Pattern matches T1110 Brute Force: many rapid failures followed by single success

recommended_actions.action: Force password reset for jsmith account
Enable MFA for all VPN accounts
Monitor jsmith account for lateral movement

title: Compromised jsmith account used for lateral movement across network
summary: jsmith's VPN account was brute-forced by attacker (ALERT-001), then successfully accessed from internal IP 10.0.1.107. Immediately after VPN login, jsmith logged into 4 hosts (WS-14, DB-01, FS-01, DC-01) within 11 minutes — highly unusual for a Marketing Coordinator whose normal hosts are WS-07 and FS-01 only. This indicates the attacker used valid credentials for lateral movement.
evidence: ALERT-001 confirmed brute force attack on jsmith VPN from malicious IP 185.220.101.47
Query logs show 6 failed VPN attempts from 185.220.101.47 between 02:14-02:18, then successful login at 02:18:24
IP 10.0.1.107 rated as internal network range
User context: jsmith is Marketing Coordinator with normal hosts WS-07 and FS-01 only, works_remote:false, not admin — accessing DC-01 and DB-01 is highly anomalous
Timeline: VPN success at 02:18:24, then lateral moves to 4 hosts within 17 minutes
related_to_prior: ALERT-001 was brute force attack on same jsmith VPN account from external IP; this alert shows successful authentication followed by lateral movement — classic attack chain where compromised credentials are used to move laterally

recommended_actions.action: Immediately isolate and investigate WS-14, DB-01, FS-01, and DC-01 for signs of compromise or persistence mechanisms
Reset jsmith's credentials and enforce MFA reset
Search for other accounts that may have received similar brute force attacks from IP 185.220.101.47
Review network segmentation — why can a marketing coordinator access DC-01 and DB-01?

title: Compromised jsmith account exfiltrating data to known C2 infrastructure
summary: The jsmith account (Marketing Coordinator) was compromised and is exfiltrating ~2.5 TB of data to external IP 45.137.21.9 via 6 HTTPS connections on port 8443. The destination IP has a malicious reputation with 88 reports as known C2/data-exfil infrastructure. This continues the attack chain from ALERT-001 (brute force) and ALERT-002 (lateral movement).
evidence: 6 firewall connections from 10.0.2.60 to 45.137.21.9 on port 8443 totaling 2,579 MB
IP reputation: 45.137.21.9 malicious, known-c2, data-exfil-infra (88 reports)
jsmith logged into FS-01 at 02:31:24 from 10.0.1.107 (consistent with compromised account)
User context: jsmith is Marketing Coordinator with normal access to FS-01
ALERT-001: Brute force on jsmith VPN account from malicious IP
ALERT-002: jsmith used for lateral movement across network
related_to_prior: Continues attack chain from ALERT-001 (brute force) and ALERT-002 (lateral movement) - same compromised jsmith account

recommended_actions.action: Immediately isolate FS-01 from network to stop ongoing exfiltration
Reset jsmith password and enforce MFA
Deploy EDR hunt for other hosts connecting to 45.137.21.9
Review jsmith's recent file access and process execution for additional indicators
